reasoning_summary:
Step-by-step verification in order, no step failed definitively.

Lines 0002-0016 (construction): h is defined edgewise from the original edges of G: for original edge (u,v), if g(u,v) >= f(u,v) put g(u,v)-f(u,v) on the forward residual arc (u,v); otherwise put f(u,v)-g(u,v) on the backward residual arc (v,u); all remaining residual arcs get 0. This is the standard 'g minus f' construction and is well defined under the residual-network convention stated in lines 0004-0005 (each original edge contributes one forward and one backward residual arc, i.e. the usual no-antiparallel-edges convention of the source text).

Lines 0017-0025 (capacity): forward case h(u,v) = g(u,v)-f(u,v) <= c(u,v)-f(u,v) = cf(u,v) uses only g(u,v) <= c(u,v); backward case h(v,u) = f(u,v)-g(u,v) <= f(u,v) = cf(v,u) uses only g(u,v) >= 0. Both nonnegativity claims follow from the case split. Correct.

Lines 0026-0058 (conservation, setup): conservation of f and g at x subtracted gives (*) sum_{y:(x->y) in E}[g(x,y)-f(x,y)] = sum_{y:(y->x) in E}[g(y,x)-f(y,x)]. Correct.

Lines 0061-0067 (key identities): for an original arc (x->y), g(x,y)-f(x,y) = h(x,y)-h(y,x); checked in both branches (g>=f gives h(x,y)=g-f, h(y,x)=0; g<f gives h(y,x)=f-g, h(x,y)=0). The mirrored identity for original arcs (y->x) is verified the same way. Correct given the one-forward/one-backward residual convention.

Lines 0068-0102 (algebra): substituting yields sum_{(x->y)}h(x,y) - sum_{(x->y)}h(y,x) = sum_{(y->x)}h(y,x) - sum_{(y->x)}h(x,y); moving the negative terms across gives exactly lines 0090-0102. I recomputed the sign bookkeeping independently and it matches.

Lines 0103-0113 (interpretation): the left side is genuinely the outflow of h at x in Gf -- forward residual arcs out of x come from original edges (x->y) and carry h(x,y); backward residual arcs out of x come from original edges (y->x) and are the arcs (x,y), carrying h(x,y). Symmetrically the right side is the inflow. So conservation of h at every x not in {s,t} holds. Correct.

Lines 0114-0158 (value): the computation |g|-|f| = sum_y [g(s,y)-f(s,y)] = sum_y h(s,y) - sum_y h(y,s) = |h| is correct. Two cosmetic imprecisions, neither of which breaks the argument: (a) line 0116 asserts s has no net inflow, effectively assuming no flow-carrying edges enter s -- but if such edges exist the same two identities give net outflow of h at s = sum_out[g-f] - sum_in[g-f] = |g|-|f| anyway, so the conclusion is unchanged; (b) line 0136's phrase 'exactly one of h(s,y) or h(y,s) is positive' fails in the tie case g(s,y) = f(s,y), where both are 0 -- but the difference identity h(s,y)-h(y,s) = g(s,y)-f(s,y) that is actually used still holds there.

The only genuine caveat is that if G contains antiparallel edges (u,v) and (v,u), the construction assigns two values to the same residual arc and the identity at line 0063 would need the net form; the proof adopts the standard convention (lines 0004-0005) under which this does not arise, matching the source text's residual-network definition. This is a convention the argument inherits, not an error in a step, and the theorem itself is true. Verdict: VALID.
